message.content: The number of mitochondria varies widely among cell types and depends on the cell’s energy demands. In most mammalian cells you’ll find roughly **50–500 mitochondria** per cell. Cells that require a lot of ATP—such as skeletal muscle fibers, cardiac myocytes, or neurons—can contain several thousand mitochondria, whereas cells with lower metabolic rates may have only a few dozen.
